categories.label: Manufacturing
categories.blurb: Machines, quality and output on the factory floor.

categories.label: Quality control
categories.blurb: Check parts and products, from photos or from line readings.

templates.name: Machine failure warning
templates.question: Which machines are likely to break down in the next 7 days, so you can service them first?
templates.predicts: Will this machine fail in the next 7 days: yes or no, and how sure.
templates.source: Your machine sensors or MES, plus the maintenance log
templates.balance: Failures are rare. Try to have at least 50 rows where the answer is yes.
tips: Use readings from before the failure, never from the day it broke.
One row per machine per day works better than one row per machine.
Leave machines out on days they were switched off.

columns.name: machine_type
columns.meaning: The model or family of the machine.

columns.name: air_temp_c
columns.meaning: Air temperature around the machine, in °C.

columns.name: speed_rpm
columns.meaning: How fast it turns, in turns per minute.

columns.name: tool_wear_min
columns.meaning: Minutes the current tool has been used.

columns.name: fails_within_7_days
columns.meaning: Did it fail in the 7 days after this day?

templates.name: Spot bad batches early
templates.question: Will this batch pass quality control, judged from the line settings while it is made?
templates.predicts: Pass or fail for each batch, before it reaches inspection.
templates.source: Line settings from the PLC or MES, plus QC results
templates.balance: Include failed batches too. A model that only sees passes cannot learn what a fail looks like.
tips: Use the settings recorded while the batch ran, not after.
Keep one supplier code per raw material as a category.

columns.name: supplier
columns.meaning: Supplier of the main raw material.

templates.name: Energy use per shift
templates.question: How many kWh will the next shift use, so you can plan load and cost?
templates.predicts: The energy one shift will use, in kWh.
templates.source: Energy meters and the production plan
templates.balance: Include quiet shifts and busy ones, so the model sees the full range.
tips: Plan numbers like planned units are fine; actual numbers from after the shift are not.

templates.name: Why did the line stop?
templates.question: When a machine stops, what is the most likely cause, so the right person is called first?
templates.predicts: One cause: mechanical, electrical, material or operator.
templates.source: Downtime log from your MES, with the cause the technician wrote down
templates.balance: Try to have at least 50 stops for each cause.
tips: Use the alarm code and readings from the moment it stopped, not the repair notes.
Merge causes that mean the same thing, like "belt" and "belt worn".

templates.name: Batch yield
templates.question: What share of a batch will be good, from the settings and materials, before it runs?
templates.predicts: Good units as a percentage of the batch.
templates.source: Batch records and the production plan
templates.balance: Include poor batches too, so the model learns what drags yield down.
tips: Record the raw material lot or grade; it often explains most of the spread.

columns.name: material_grade
columns.meaning: Grade of the main raw material.

columns.name: yield_pct
columns.meaning: Good units as a % of the batch.

templates.name: Tool change due
templates.question: Should this cutting tool be changed before the next job, before it ruins parts?
templates.predicts: Change the tool now: yes or no.
templates.source: CNC controller logs and tool change records
templates.balance: Rows where a change was needed are fewer; aim for 100 or more.
tips: Spindle load creeping up is usually the first sign; log it every job.

columns.name: change_needed
columns.meaning: Was the tool worn out at the next check?

templates.name: Surface defect check
templates.question: Look at a photo of a part and say if it is fine or has a scratch, dent or stain.
templates.predicts: One answer per photo: ok, scratch, dent or stain, with how sure.
templates.source: A camera at the inspection station, or phone photos from inspectors
templates.balance: Defects are rare. Keep taking photos of defects until each folder has at least 100.
tips: Same camera, same angle, same light for every photo.
Fill the frame with the part; crop out the conveyor.
Include borderline parts that inspectors argued about.

folders.name: stain
folders.meaning: Parts with a stain or mark.

templates.name: Circuit board solder check
templates.question: Look at a close-up of a solder joint and say if it is good or which fault it has.
templates.predicts: Good, bridge, missing or cold joint, for each photo.
templates.row_means: One close-up photo of one joint.
templates.source: Your AOI machine images, or a microscope camera
templates.balance: At least 100 photos of each fault.
tips: Crop each photo to one joint; the model learns faster.
Keep the board the same way up in every photo.

templates.name: Weld seam inspection
templates.question: Check a photo of a weld for porosity, cracks or undercut before the part moves on.
templates.predicts: Good, porosity, crack or undercut, for each photo.
templates.row_means: One photo of one weld seam.
templates.source: Camera on the welding cell, or photos from the weld inspector
templates.balance: Cracks are rare; collect them over several weeks.
tips: Clean the seam before the photo; spatter confuses the model.
Use a diffuser so the metal does not glare.

templates.name: Packaging and label check
templates.question: Before boxes leave the line, check that the label is there, readable and the box is not torn.
templates.predicts: Ok, misprint, torn or no label, for each photo.
templates.row_means: One photo of one box or pack.
templates.source: A camera at the end of the packing line
templates.balance: You can stage bad examples on purpose: tear a few empty boxes, print a few bad labels.
tips: Photograph the side where the label goes, every time.

folders.name: misprint
folders.meaning: Label smudged, cut off or wrong.

templates.name: Fruit and produce grading
templates.question: Grade fruit or vegetables from a photo so sorting is the same on every shift.
templates.predicts: Grade A, grade B or reject, for each photo.
templates.row_means: One photo of one piece of produce.
templates.source: Photos from the sorting table
templates.balance: Have graders agree on the folders first; the model copies their judgement.
tips: Use a plain background in one colour.
Photograph both sides if bruises can be on either.

templates.name: Out of tolerance warning
templates.question: Will this machined part be out of tolerance, judged from the machine settings before measuring?
templates.predicts: Out of tolerance: yes or no, and how likely.
templates.source: CNC logs plus your CMM measurement results
templates.balance: Out-of-tolerance parts are rare; 100 or more makes the model useful.
tips: Room temperature matters for tight tolerances; log it.

templates.name: Lead scoring
templates.question: Which new leads are most likely to become customers, so sales calls them first?
templates.predicts: Will this lead become a customer: yes or no, and how likely.
templates.source: Your CRM export, like HubSpot or Salesforce
templates.balance: Only use leads old enough to have a final answer, for example 90 days or older.
tips: Count activity from before the deal was decided, not after.
Group rare industries into "other" so each group has enough rows.

columns.name: pages_viewed
columns.meaning: Pages they looked at on your site.

templates.name: Deal win chance
templates.question: How likely is each open deal to close, so the forecast is honest?
templates.predicts: Will this deal be won: yes or no, and how likely.
templates.source: Closed deals from your CRM
templates.balance: Use deals that are already won or lost. Open deals have no answer yet.
tips: Take each deal as it looked at the same stage, for example when the proposal was sent.

templates.name: Account renewal risk
templates.question: Which business accounts may not renew, so success can step in early?
templates.predicts: Will this account renew: yes or no, and how likely.
templates.row_means: One account at 90 days before renewal.
templates.source: Billing system plus product usage
templates.balance: Accounts that left are usually few. 30 or more is a good start.
tips: Measure usage in the 30 days before the snapshot date.

columns.name: active_users_30d
columns.meaning: People who used it in the last 30 days.

columns.name: tickets_90d
columns.meaning: Support tickets in the last 90 days.

templates.name: Upsell chance
templates.question: Which customers are ready for a bigger plan or more seats, so account managers call the right ones?
templates.predicts: Will this account upgrade in the next 90 days: yes or no, and how likely.
templates.source: Billing system plus product usage
templates.balance: Upgrades are usually few; 50 or more is a good start.
tips: Seat usage near 100% is a strong sign; include it as a percentage.

columns.name: months_customer
columns.meaning: How long they have been a customer.

columns.name: meetings_90d
columns.meaning: Meetings with your team in 90 days.

templates.name: Campaign response
templates.question: Which accounts will respond to the next campaign, so you send it to fewer people and get more replies?
templates.predicts: Will this contact respond: yes or no, and how likely.
templates.row_means: One contact in one past campaign.
templates.source: Your marketing tool, like HubSpot, Mailchimp or Marketo
templates.balance: Replies are rare. Use several past campaigns to get 200 or more.
tips: A reply, a meeting or a form fill all count as yes; pick one rule and keep it.

templates.name: Best way to reach
templates.question: For each contact, which channel gets an answer: email, a call, LinkedIn or an event invite?
templates.predicts: One channel: email, call, linkedin or event.
templates.row_means: One contact, with the channel that first got a reply.
templates.source: CRM activity history
templates.balance: Try to have at least 100 contacts for each channel.
tips: Only use contacts who replied; the answer is the channel they replied on.

columns.name: linkedin_connected
columns.meaning: Connected to your team on LinkedIn?

columns.name: best_channel
columns.meaning: Channel that first got a reply.

templates.name: Next-quarter revenue per account
templates.question: How much will each account spend next quarter, so sales targets and forecasts are realistic?
templates.predicts: Revenue from this account next quarter.
templates.source: Billing history plus the CRM pipeline
templates.balance: At least four quarters of history per account helps.
tips: Use open pipeline as it stood at the start of the quarter, not the end.

columns.name: seats
columns.meaning: Paid seats at the start of the quarter.

columns.name: revenue_same_q_last_year
columns.meaning: Revenue in the same quarter a year ago.

columns.name: open_pipeline
columns.meaning: Value of open deals for this account.

columns.name: active_users_30d
columns.meaning: Active users in the last 30 days.

templates.name: Subscriber churn
templates.question: Which subscribers are about to cancel, so you can send the right offer?
templates.predicts: Will this person cancel next month: yes or no, and how likely.
templates.source: Subscription and billing data
templates.balance: If fewer than 1 in 20 cancel, add more months of history.
tips: Payment failures are often the strongest sign; include them if you can.

columns.name: months_subscribed
columns.meaning: How long they have been a subscriber.

columns.name: logins_30d
columns.meaning: Times they used it in the last 30 days.

columns.name: payment_failed
columns.meaning: Did a payment fail this month?

columns.name: cancelled_next_month
columns.meaning: Did they cancel in the next month?

templates.name: Will they buy again
templates.question: Which shoppers will order again in the next 30 days, and who needs a nudge?
templates.predicts: Will this shopper order again within 30 days.
templates.source: Your shop orders table
templates.balance: Pick a date at least 30 days ago so every row has an answer.
tips: Days since last order beats the order date itself; the template uses that.

columns.name: used_voucher
columns.meaning: Did they use a voucher last time?

columns.name: ordered_within_30d
columns.meaning: Did they order in the next 30 days?

templates.name: Fake listing check
templates.question: For a marketplace where people sell to people: which new listings look like scams?
templates.predicts: Is this listing likely fake: yes or no, and how likely.
templates.source: Your listings table plus moderation decisions
templates.balance: Fake listings are rare. Collect at least 100 confirmed ones.
tips: Price compared to similar items is a strong sign; the template asks for it as a ratio.

columns.name: price_vs_typical
columns.meaning: Price divided by the usual price of similar items.

columns.name: seller_rating
columns.meaning: Seller rating from 0 to 5; 0 if none.

templates.name: Loan default risk
templates.question: How likely is a borrower to miss payments, from what you know when they apply?
templates.predicts: Will this loan default: yes or no, and how likely.
templates.row_means: One loan, as it looked when approved.
templates.source: Loan applications and repayment history
templates.balance: Only use loans that have finished or are long enough in to know.
tips: Check local rules before using personal data such as age or gender. The template leaves them out.

columns.name: debt_to_income
columns.meaning: Monthly debt divided by monthly income.

columns.name: late_payments_2y
columns.meaning: Late payments in the last 2 years.

templates.name: Payment fraud check
templates.question: Is this card or wallet payment likely fraud, so it can be held for review?
templates.predicts: Is this payment fraud: yes or no, and how likely.
templates.source: Payment logs plus chargebacks
templates.balance: Fraud is very rare. Aim for 200 or more confirmed fraud rows.
tips: Mark a payment as fraud only once a chargeback or review confirms it.

columns.name: km_from_usual
columns.meaning: Distance from where they usually pay.

columns.name: payments_last_hour
columns.meaning: Payments by this person in the last hour.

templates.name: Late invoice payment
templates.question: Which invoices will be paid late, so finance can follow up before the due date?
templates.predicts: Will this invoice be paid late: yes or no.
templates.source: Accounting system, like Xero, Jurnal or SAP
templates.balance: Use invoices that are already paid, so every row has an answer.
tips: The customer’s past average delay is usually the strongest column.

columns.name: customer_avg_days_late
columns.meaning: How late this customer paid before, on average.

columns.name: paid_late
columns.meaning: Was it paid after the due date?

templates.name: Who might leave
templates.question: Which employees are at risk of leaving in the next year, so managers can have the talk early?
templates.predicts: Will this person leave within 12 months: yes or no, and how likely.
templates.source: Your HR system plus engagement survey
templates.balance: If very few people left, add more years of history.
tips: Keep results private to HR. Use them to start conversations, not to make decisions alone.
The template leaves out age, gender and other protected traits on purpose.

templates.name: Offer acceptance
templates.question: Will the candidate accept the offer, so recruiters know when to keep a backup?
templates.predicts: Will this offer be accepted: yes or no.
templates.source: Your applicant tracking system
templates.balance: Include declined offers; they teach the most.
tips: Offer compared to what they asked for works better than the raw salary.

columns.name: offer_vs_ask
columns.meaning: Offer divided by what they asked for.

columns.name: days_to_offer
columns.meaning: Days from first interview to offer.

templates.name: Time to fill a job
templates.question: How many days will it take to hire for this opening, so managers can plan cover?
templates.predicts: Days from opening the job to an accepted offer.
templates.row_means: One job opening that was filled.
templates.source: Your applicant tracking system
templates.balance: Leave out openings that were cancelled.
tips: Salary compared to the market matters more than the salary itself.

columns.name: salary_vs_market
columns.meaning: Offered salary divided by the market rate.

columns.name: days_to_fill
columns.meaning: Days until an offer was accepted.

templates.name: Training completion
templates.question: Who is likely not to finish an assigned course, so they get a reminder or help in time?
templates.predicts: Will this person finish the course on time: yes or no.
templates.source: Your learning system (LMS)
templates.balance: Use courses whose deadline has passed.
tips: Course length in hours is usually a strong column.

columns.name: past_courses_done_pct
columns.meaning: Share of their past courses finished, as a %.

columns.name: completed_on_time
columns.meaning: Did they finish by the deadline?

templates.name: Safety incident risk
templates.question: Which teams or shifts are at higher risk of a safety incident in the next 90 days?
templates.predicts: Incident in the next 90 days: yes or no, and how likely.
templates.row_means: One team on one site in one month.
templates.source: HSE incident log plus rosters and training records
templates.balance: Count near misses too; they give the model far more to learn from.
tips: Use this to target safety walks and training, never to blame a person.

columns.name: overtime_hours_week
columns.meaning: Average overtime per person per week.

columns.name: new_staff_pct
columns.meaning: Share of people under 6 months in role, as a %.

columns.name: safety_training_pct
columns.meaning: Share with current safety training, as a %.

columns.name: incident_next_90d
columns.meaning: Was there an incident in the next 90 days?

templates.name: Safety gear check
templates.question: From a photo at a site entrance, is the person wearing a helmet and a vest?
templates.predicts: Full gear, no helmet or no vest, for each photo.
templates.row_means: One photo of one person at the entrance.
templates.source: Photos from an entrance camera
templates.balance: Stage the "no helmet" and "no vest" photos with volunteers if real ones are rare.
tips: Tell people the camera is there and why. Check your local privacy rules first.
Do not keep the photos longer than you need to teach the model.

templates.name: Late delivery warning
templates.question: Which shipments will miss their promised date, so you can tell the customer early?
templates.predicts: Will this shipment arrive late: yes or no, and how likely.
templates.source: Your shipping or TMS export
templates.balance: Use delivered shipments only.
tips: Add the carrier as a category; it often matters more than distance.

columns.name: arrived_late
columns.meaning: Did it arrive after the promise?

templates.name: Weekly demand
templates.question: How many units of each product will sell next week, so you order the right amount?
templates.predicts: Units sold next week, per product and store.
templates.row_means: One product in one store in one week.
templates.source: Sales history from your POS or shop
templates.balance: At least one year of weeks helps the model see seasons.
tips: Mark promotion weeks; they explain most spikes.

columns.name: units_same_week_last_year
columns.meaning: Units sold in the same week a year ago.

columns.name: on_promo
columns.meaning: Is it on promotion next week?

templates.name: Ticket escalation risk
templates.question: Which support tickets are likely to escalate or end in a complaint?
templates.predicts: Will this ticket escalate: yes or no, and how likely.
templates.row_means: One ticket after its first reply.
templates.source: Your helpdesk, like Zendesk or Freshdesk
templates.balance: Use closed tickets so every row has an answer.
tips: First reply time is usually the strongest column.

columns.name: previous_tickets_90d
columns.meaning: Tickets from this customer in 90 days.

templates.name: Route tickets to the right team
templates.question: Which team should handle a new ticket, from its details?
templates.predicts: One of your teams: billing, technical, delivery or account.
templates.source: Your helpdesk, with the team that solved it
templates.balance: Try to have at least 100 rows for each team.
tips: Today this uses ticket details, not the words in the message. Reading the message text comes later.

columns.name: has_order_id
columns.meaning: Did they include an order number?

templates.name: Product photo category
templates.question: When a seller uploads a photo, suggest the right category so listings are easier to find.
templates.predicts: One category per photo, like shoes, bags, phones or clothing.
templates.source: Photos from your listings, with the category they ended up in
templates.balance: Start with your 10 to 20 biggest categories; add more later.
tips: Use the main photo of each listing, not the extra ones.
Drop photos that are mostly text or screenshots.

templates.name: Sort scanned documents
templates.question: Sort scans and phone photos of documents into the right pile before anyone reads them.
templates.predicts: Invoice, receipt, ID card or bank statement, for each image.
templates.source: Your document inbox or scanner folder
templates.balance: Mix scans and phone photos, since both will arrive later.
tips: Blur or remove ID numbers in the example set if you share it.
Use the first page only.

templates.name: Damaged parcel photos
templates.question: From a photo at the dock, is this parcel damaged and needs a closer look?
templates.predicts: Intact or damaged, for each photo.
templates.source: Dock camera or photos taken by couriers
templates.balance: Damaged parcels are rare; keep collecting until there are 150.
tips: Photograph the worst side of the parcel.
Keep the barcode in view so you can match the photo later.

templates.name: Review mood
templates.question: Read each customer review and say if it is positive, neutral or negative, so unhappy customers get a reply first.
templates.predicts: Positive, neutral or negative, for each review.
templates.source: Reviews from your shop, app store or marketplace
templates.balance: Neutral reviews are often few; try to have at least 100.
tips: Keep the review as the customer wrote it; spelling mistakes are fine.
Mixed languages are fine if the real reviews are mixed too.

columns.name: review_text
examples: Box arrived crushed, no reply from seller
It is ok for the price

templates.name: Fake listing check with photos
templates.question: For a marketplace where people sell to people: use the listing photo, title and price together to spot scams.
templates.predicts: Is this listing likely fake: yes or no, and how likely.
templates.row_means: One listing, with its main photo.
templates.source: Your listings table, the listing photos and moderation decisions
templates.balance: Collect at least 100 confirmed fake listings, with their photos.
tips: Stock photos copied from the web are a strong sign; keep the photo as uploaded.
Use the main photo only.

columns.name: photo
columns.meaning: File name of the main photo, inside the photos folder.

columns.name: price_vs_typical
columns.meaning: Price divided by the usual price of similar items.

templates.name: Lead scoring from call notes
templates.question: Use what the sales rep wrote after the first call, plus the basics, to say which leads will buy.
templates.predicts: Will this lead become a customer: yes or no, and how likely.
templates.row_means: One lead, with the notes from the first call.
templates.source: Call notes and leads from your CRM
templates.balance: Only use leads old enough to have a final answer.
tips: Use the notes from the first call only, before anyone knew the outcome.

columns.name: call_notes
columns.meaning: What the rep wrote after the first call.
examples: Budget approved for Q1, wants a demo for the IT team
Just browsing, call back next year
Comparing us with two others, price sensitive

templates.name: Employee feedback topics
templates.question: Sort open comments from engagement surveys into topics, so HR sees what people talk about most.
templates.predicts: One topic per comment: pay, manager, workload, growth or tools.
templates.source: Open answers from your engagement survey
templates.balance: Have two people agree on the topic for a few hundred comments first.
tips: Remove names from the comments before teaching.
Keep results to whole teams, never single people.

columns.name: comment
examples: I have not had a raise in two years
Too many meetings, no time for real work

templates.name: Sort maintenance requests
templates.question: Read a maintenance request as the operator wrote it and send it to the right specialist.
templates.predicts: Mechanical, electrical, hydraulic or software, for each request.
templates.source: Your maintenance system (CMMS) work orders
templates.balance: At least 100 requests for each kind of fault.
tips: Use the text as the operator first typed it, not the technician’s report.

columns.name: request_text
examples: Loud grinding noise from the gearbox
Oil on the floor under press 2

templates.name: Defect check with line details
templates.question: Use the part photo together with the line, shift and inspector note to sort defects more reliably than the photo alone.
templates.predicts: Ok, scratch, dent or stain, for each part.
templates.row_means: One part: its photo plus the line details.
templates.source: Inspection camera photos plus your MES records
templates.balance: At least 100 parts for each defect, each with its photo.
tips: The photo file name must match a file in the photos folder exactly.
Notes can be empty; the model still uses the photo.

columns.name: photo
columns.meaning: File name of the part photo, inside the photos folder.

columns.name: inspector_note
columns.meaning: What the inspector wrote, if anything.

templates.name: Warranty and insurance claim check
templates.question: Use the damage photo, the customer’s description and the claim details together to flag claims that need a closer look.
templates.predicts: Needs review: yes or no, and how likely.
templates.row_means: One claim, with one damage photo.
templates.source: Your claims system plus the photos customers upload
templates.balance: Use decided claims only; aim for 100 or more that needed review.
tips: Use the first photo the customer sent.
Check local rules on automated decisions; use this to sort, not to reject.

columns.name: damage_photo
columns.meaning: File name of the damage photo.

columns.name: description
examples: Water damage, phone fell in the pool

columns.name: needs_review
columns.meaning: Did it turn out to need a closer look?

templates.name: Route tickets from the message
templates.question: Read what the customer wrote and send the ticket to the right team, without anyone sorting by hand.
templates.predicts: Billing, technical, delivery or account, for each ticket.
templates.source: Your helpdesk, with the team that solved it
templates.balance: Try to have at least 100 tickets for each team.
tips: Use the customer’s first message only.
Remove email signatures if you can; they add noise.

columns.name: message
examples: I see two payments for order 4471
Since the update the app closes when I log in
It said 2 days, it has been 6
